name: MI-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: Moss's large fundraising advantage over Baker
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
Open seat removes incumbency but not the partisan baseline
model.rationale: The district's D+9 lean plus a favorable national environment points to a solid Democratic hold, and Jeremy Moss has outraised Ethan Baker roughly ten to one with outside support on his side. Markets price a Democratic win near 95%, consistent with a Safe D rating despite the open seat.
model.watch: A major Republican outside-spending surge or a polling surprise showing single digits would move this toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Haley Stevens (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Haley Stevens's retirement leaves this Detroit-area district open, but its D+9 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic column territory. State Senator Jeremy Moss enters the general with a decisive financial edge, having raised about $1.5 million to Ethan Baker's roughly $142,000, and he benefits from nearly $300,000 in outside support. Baker has modest resources and no visible outside backing.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee about a 95% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, which point to a comfortable Democratic hold in the high teens.
